summary: Builder of the Joshua Smith House at Hauppauge, home to four generations of his family; John's 2nd cousin 9 times removed.
bio: Joshua Smith (1732–1814) built the Joshua Smith House at Hauppauge. Accounts of its date differ: one puts it about 1769, not far west of Thomas Wheeler's at the old store and post-office corner, while a family scrapbook dates the salt-box house to about 1761 or possibly earlier, the year of Joshua's marriage in October 1761. Four generations of the family lived there: Joshua himself, Judge Joshua Smith II, Senator Joshua B. Smith and Ellen. The house was remodeled in 1819 and demolished in 1960; the woodwork of its hall is now preserved at the Henry Francis duPont Winterthur Museum. He is John's 2nd cousin 9 times removed.

Four generations lived there: Joshua I, Judge Joshua II, Sen. Joshua B., Ellen. No Find a Grave memorial found for him.
